bullets.title: Monday's AI rally fades Tuesday; semis/tech giving back 4-7% on hawkish Fed
bullets.body: After Monday's historic session (S&P +4.73%, NDX +6.9%, best day in 19 months driven by Jensen Huang's reinstatement), Tuesday pre-market sees broad reversal: NVDA -5.6%, AMD -4.9%, MU -6.9%, SNDK -7.0%, HPE -12%, DELL -7%, SMH -4%. S&P 500 futures -0.9%, Nasdaq 100 futures -1.6%. NDX 5%+ days historically rare and occurred at key market pivots, not necessarily sustained breakouts.

bullets.title: Fed's Williams doubles down on tightening; financial conditions at tariff-war levels
bullets.body: NY Fed President Williams reiterated inflation must return to 2% 'in timely manner and on sustained basis,' refusing to rule out consecutive rate hikes. Financial conditions have tightened to levels last seen during the tariff war, with Morgan Stanley quant noting the strongest negative daily correlation between FCI changes and Tech sector contributions to S&P 500 returns. JPMorgan's 2027 outlook calls for 75bp of additional Fed hikes through Q1'27, with 10-year yields rising to 5.10%.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as NVDA CEO — relief bounce, not a game-changer
bullets.body: Trump lobbied the NVDA board; VP Vance cited DoJ's no-wrongdoing finding. Investors broadly view the news as a relief rally rather than a catalyst: implied real yields rose despite the news, hedge fund net buying was only +0.9std, and multiple sell-side analysts note lingering overhangs — chip export controls, congressional scrutiny (Huang testifies before Senate Banking Dec 3), Singapore's Megaspeed probe, and AI capex ROI concerns. Semiconductor positioning remains historically light, leaving room for further upside if macro cooperates.

bullets.title: NVDA export control risks intensifying: Megaspeed blacklisted, lawmakers push NDAA controls
bullets.body: The US officially blacklisted Megaspeed and six other Southeast Asian companies for export control violations tied to the NVDA espionage probe. Bipartisan lawmakers are pushing tighter chip export controls into the must-pass NDAA with expectations of a veto-proof majority. China extended its suspension of critical mineral export bans (gallium, germanium) through January 27. Congressional pressure on the MATCH Act and NDAA will intensify following Huang's return.

bullets.title: AI token pricing collapsing; average cost/million tokens fell 21% last month
bullets.body: One analyst argues that declining token prices (avg price/million tokens -21% in past month, with new entrants set to accelerate declines) threaten chip industry pricing power and GPU spending durability. AI spend remains concentrated in <1% of businesses, failing to proliferate broadly beyond VC-backed tech/finance/services. If equities rally on AI optimism, the offset mechanism is likely higher yields/stronger dollar rather than easing financial conditions.

bullets.title: SOX valuation only 10-15% above 2018/COVID troughs — tactical bottom signals emerging
bullets.body: UBS notes semiconductor valuations are within historical range and only 10-15% above prior cycle troughs, suggesting a tactical bottom may be forming. However, broad data center estimate cuts were not reversed by the Jensen news — UBS frames the chip supply gap as a supply-side issue, not a demand collapse. Semiconductor positioning is below July lows, leaving room for a squeeze if the rally continues.

bullets.title: UBS flags 'buy the dip vs. caution' debate: valuations adjusted but sentiment not at extremes
bullets.body: UBS is hosting a conference call examining whether the selloff has created a buyable dip. Key questions: whether bonds are beginning to hedge equities again, whether credit yields are now attractive, and whether gold is oversold/dollar overbought. Valuations have adjusted significantly, but sentiment is not yet at panic extremes.

bullets.title: RBC sets S&P 500 12-month target at 8,050 (16.5% upside); prefers Value over Growth
bullets.body: RBC's equity strategy call projects 8,050 on the S&P 500 over 12 months. The firm prefers Value over Growth and Small over Large. Monday's breadth was overwhelming: 85% of S&P, 95% of NDX, and 97% of IGV closed higher; S&P Info Tech surged +9.1% and Comm Services +5.2%.

bullets.title: JPMorgan 2027 rates outlook: Fed hikes 75bp through Q1, 10yr to 5.10%, then fades
bullets.body: JPM forecasts the Fed delivers cumulative 100bp of additional tightening through Q1'27, with 2- and 10-year Treasury yields peaking at 4.90% and 5.10% respectively, before declining to 4.60%/4.95% by YE27. IG spreads expected to tighten to 90bp (7.1% total return), HY to 365bp (8.5% return). Debt ceiling becomes binding in late-February 2027 with x-date estimated November 2027.

bullets.title: 80-90% of cyberattacks now AI-generated; enterprise security budgets shifting toward DSPM/DLP
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's AI risk webcast highlighted that 80-90% of cybersecurity attacks are now AI-generated, with attack costs trending toward $0. Autonomous AI agent breaches are raising new concerns. Enterprise budget priorities are shifting toward Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) and Data Loss Prevention (DLP). CrowdStrike's Kurtz noted ~25% of all historically identified vulnerabilities were discovered this year, with October discoveries up 300% y/y.

bullets.title: Optical/datacom TAM upgraded to $88B by 2030; CPO/integrated optics to be ~28% of market
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its Datacom TAM estimate to $88B by 2030 (from $70B prior), implying ~20% CAGR. 800G optics peak in 2028 near $40B; 1.6T ramps at 50% CAGR. Integrated optics (CPO+NPO) reach $25B by 2030. Optical Circuit Switching triples to $8B+ by 2031 with Google as anchor buyer. JPM rates CIEN and CRDO overweight in the space.

bullets.title: Retail earnings broadly strong: BBY +6.1% comp, ANF +6%, DLTR +4.6% traffic-driven
bullets.body: Pre-market retail prints are broadly positive: BBY beat by 380bps on comps with raised FY guidance; ANF beat by 240bps with FY EPS raised to $13.70-$13.90 and revenue growth guidance to +6%; DLTR delivered 4.6% comps on 3.8% traffic acceleration with FY'26 EPS raised to $8.05-$8.25. Results suggest the consumer remains more resilient than macro headwinds imply, though tariff refunds boosted several prints.

bullets.title: Hedgeye maintains Quad 4 crash signal; copper -4%, UST 10yr breaks key TREND levels
bullets.body: Hedgeye keeps its Quad 4 crash signal on NVDA and Tech broadly, noting copper fell another 4% signaling continued AI bubble deflation. The 10-year UST yield broke both TRADE (5.06%) and TREND (4.94%) support levels. QQQ implied vol trades at an 18% discount to 30-day realized, flagging extreme complacency. Hedgeye recommends long TLT/bond proxies (XLU, XLP) and short Energy, Lithium, Silver, DRAM, and neocloud.

bullets.title: November payrolls preview: Wolfe sees 85k vs. 93k consensus; unlikely to shift Fed path
bullets.body: Wolfe forecasts November NFP at 85k (vs. 93k consensus) with unemployment steady at 4.1% and AHE +0.29% MoM. A print below 20k or unemployment above 4.3% would be needed to materially trim rate-hike expectations — suggesting this week's jobs data is unlikely to be a macro catalyst either way. YoY wage trend estimated at 3.0%, below the 3.5-4.0% range consistent with 2% inflation.

bullets.title: CRWD/ZS M&A expected to accelerate cybersecurity consolidation; OKTA, NTSK, SAIL flagged as targets
bullets.body: Following CRWD's $43.9B all-stock acquisition of Zscaler, RBC and Morgan Stanley both expect an accelerated M&A cycle in cybersecurity, driven by agentic AI threat complexity and platform consolidation logic. OKTA, NTSK, and SAIL are flagged as top strategic takeout candidates; RPD and QLYS as PE candidates. The deal expands CRWD's TAM by $185B by CY29 and targets ~$1B annualized revenue synergies by 30 months post-close.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples compressed: IGV -9.5% YTD vs. S&P +10.5%; All-SaaS at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: Wolfe's SaaS tracker shows the All-SaaS index at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales (down 3.6% WoW), All-Security at 8.1x (down 7.5% WoW), and All-Vertical at 6.9x (up 2.4% WoW). IGV has returned -9.5% YTD vs. S&P 500 at +10.5% YTD, underscoring the magnitude of the growth/software de-rating relative to the broader market.

bullets.title: AMZN acquires Decart for ~$7.5B to boost AWS Trainium utilization and AI inference efficiency
bullets.body: Amazon is acquiring Decart, whose optimization stack (DOS) achieved 80%+ Model FLOPS Utilization on Trainium3 vs. a 40-50% industry average. With inference now >50% of AWS AI revenue, the deal is aimed at making Trainium competitive at external sales (planned late 2027). Citi reiterates Buy on AMZN with a $350 PT and projects AWS reaching $1T in revenue by 2032 at a 33.5% CAGR.

bullets.title: Apple flagged as key beneficiary of enterprise on-device AI and local sovereignty trend
bullets.body: CrowdStrike's CEO George Kurtz highlighted Apple as a major beneficiary of accelerating local AI adoption, citing Mac Studio capabilities and enterprise demand for AI sovereignty and data privacy. On-device AI is expected to grow significantly over the next year, leveraging underutilized compute capacity while easing GPU and power constraints — a structural tailwind for AAPL hardware.

bullets.title: Robotics/Physical AI entering acceleration phase; JPM raises Unitree PT 50%, upgrades UBTech
bullets.body: JPMorgan flagged the robotics and physical AI sector as entering an acceleration phase: Unitree PT raised to Rmb1,060 (~50% upside) and UBTech upgraded to OW with HK$77 PT (~30% upside). Separately, Nuro, Lucid, and Uber began driverless testing on Bay Area public roads, with a Q1 2027 public launch expected.

bullets.title: DELL earnings tonight are key AI server catalyst; setup stronger than consensus
bullets.body: UBS sees DELL October quarter revenue potentially exceeding $51B (+4% vs. $49.9B consensus), with AI server revenue reaching $21B+ vs. $19B guide. FY27 AI server guidance could rise to $80B+ from $74B; FY27 EPS potentially ~$27 vs. $25.50 prior. Consensus expects $49.32B revenue and $6.60 EPS per the earnings calendar. This is the next major data point for the AI infrastructure demand narrative.
